newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP says interested in UK acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP says interested in UK acquisitions.

text.p: The Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) managing director George Trumbull said on Monday the AMP was interested in a number of acquisition opportunities in the U.K. following the failure of its bid for Scottish Amicable.

Asked at a news conference if the AMP was looking at acquiring Australian insurance group, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, Trumbull said: "We haven't looked at it. We would look at it if it was for sale."
"We think there are other things in the U.K. that we find fairly attractive," Trumbull said.
Trumbull declined to elaborate on prospects in the U.K..
He said the most attractive aspect of Australia for AMP was the opportunity to grow the core businesses of superannuation and retail financial services.
AMP also wanted to turn around its general insurance business, which did not provide an adequate return in 1996, he said.
"Our ability to acquire things in Australia would be limited to very small acquisitions by virtue, to some extent, of our market size and share," Trumbull said.
"Making small acquisitions doesn't have a high level of attractiveness," he said.
Trumbull said AMP believed there were good opportunities to build businesses over the long term in the Asia/Pacific region, though not necessarily for acquisitions.
"I think we have to recognise that business in the Asia/Pacific, in developing countries, won't produce a profit in my tenure as the chief executive," he said.
Trumbull said AMP expected to be in four or five Asian countries within five years, and nominated India, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand and China as attractive.
AMP was already operating in Indonesia and had a representative office in China.
"We're doing evaluations of the others and we'll probably set up representative offices in the next year," he said.
AMP believed it needed to be on the ground to do business and was looking at some joint ventures, he added.
